h1: Creating Child-Friendly Play Zones in Residential Areas

props.title: Creating Child-Friendly Play Zones in Residential Areas
props.summaryText: What makes a residential play zone genuinely child-friendly: a safe location, zones by age, the right equipment and surfaces, and the small comforts that bring families out every evening.
props.author: ananya-kulkarni
props.imageAlt: Children playing on colourful equipment at a residential play area

takeaways.text: A child-friendly play zone is safe to reach, visible from homes and separated from traffic.
Separate areas for toddlers and older children keep both safe and happy.
Shade, seating and lighting decide whether families actually use it.
Involve residents and children in choices; they will look after it better.

faq.q: What makes a play zone child-friendly?
faq.a: A safe route to reach it, separation from traffic and parking, visibility from homes, equipment for different ages, impact-absorbing surfaces, shade, seating for adults, lighting and good maintenance.

faq.q: Where should a play zone be located in a residential area?
faq.a: Centrally, visible from homes and walkways, away from driveways, parking and the main gate, with good drainage and some shade.
